questions.explain: The tropylium cation C₇H₇⁺ is planar, fully conjugated and has 6 π electrons (4n + 2). The two other ions have 4 π electrons (antiaromatic), and COT is tub-shaped (non-aromatic).

questions.q: Which statement about cyclooctatetraene (COT) is correct?
options: It is planar and antiaromatic with 8 π electrons
It is tub-shaped and non-aromatic; with potassium it gives a planar, aromatic C₈H₈²⁻
It is aromatic because it is a cyclic polyene
Its dianion has 10 π electrons and is antiaromatic
questions.explain: COT avoids antiaromaticity by adopting a tub shape, so it is non-aromatic; adding two electrons gives the planar 10π dianion, which obeys Hückel's rule.

questions.q: Which order of stability is generally correct?
questions.explain: Aromatic rings gain extra stability, antiaromatic ones (planar, 4n π) are destabilised, and non-aromatic compounds sit in between.

[18]Annulene is large enough to hold its inner H atoms while staying flat and has 18 π electrons. [10]annulene also has a Hückel count but cannot be planar, so it is non-aromatic: the trap is to count electrons without checking planarity.
